note: The corpus had no overloaded cell, so C-7's implicit check (flags bit0 <=> dc > 1.0) could not be escaped by DROPPING the flag -- only by inverting it, which is why MC68-M2 had to invert (MC68_BSI.md section 10 revision 10). This fixture stands on the line: same cantilever as C4-cantilever-selfweight, plus a 2 MN station load at block 2 (s = 0.5, NOT an end block, so it is a station load and needs no MC64). Root bending is then ~40x the self-weight moment and the screen must report dc > 1. The D/C VALUE is engine-defined (BSI B.6: capability-named, never compared across engines) so nothing here asserts a number for it -- only that it crossed 1 and that the flag agrees.

assert.note: independent of the D/C definition: statics says the reaction carries self-weight plus the applied load
THE point of this case. Every other corpus world sits far below 1, so 'never set the overloaded flag' was indistinguishable from correct behaviour.
bit0 overloaded; bit1 indicative is 0 for a frame member
blocks are in canonical order, so index 1 is the root steel cell at (0,0,0); index 0 is the ground record
